genZNote: That terminal spore gives the classic drumstick appearance. Tiny structure, very memorable exam question.

morphology.shape: Rod (bacillus) — terminal spore gives a 'drumstick' or 'tennis racket' appearance

habitat.hostAssociation: Environmental organism; causes disease after spores contaminate a wound
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Ubiquitous in soil, especially with organic or fecal contamination
habitat.reservoir: Soil; animal and human intestinal tract as the spore form

microscopy.appearance: Gram-positive rods with round terminal spores, giving a 'drumstick' appearance

culture.growthCharacteristics: Obligate anaerobe, requires strict anaerobic culture conditions
culture.colonyMorphology: Thin, spreading (swarming) colonies with irregular edges

identificationClues: Gram-positive rod with a round terminal spore, giving a 'drumstick'/'tennis racket' appearance
Diagnosis is primarily clinical (trismus/lockjaw, muscle rigidity) rather than culture-based, since wound cultures are often negative

diseases: Tetanus — generalized muscle rigidity, lockjaw/trismus, spasms
virulenceFactors: Tetanospasmin (tetanus toxin) — blocks inhibitory neurotransmitter release, causing sustained muscle contraction
clinicalImportance.transmission: Spores introduced into deep, devitalized wounds such as puncture wounds or contaminated cuts; not spread person to person
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Rare in regions with widespread vaccination using tetanus toxoid; remains a concern after trauma in unvaccinated or under-vaccinated individuals, and as neonatal tetanus via umbilical stump contamination in some resource-limited settings
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; wound Gram stain and culture can support but not rule out the diagnosis, since the organism may not always be recovered

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Not primarily diagnosed by biochemical testing — diagnosis is clinical
examFacts.importantTest: Clinical diagnosis; wound Gram stain may show terminal-spore rods
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Terminal round spore, obligate anaerobe, produces tetanospasmin
